title: Choose Whom You Will Serve
backstory: The fighting was over, and Joshua had given the whole land to the tribes as their inheritance (Joshua 11:23). He was old now, and his warning was not about Canaan's armies but about Canaan's gods: do not serve them, do not bow down to them (Joshua 23:1-7). So he gathered every tribe to Shechem one last time (Joshua 24:1) and asked them to choose.

passages.synopsis: When enemies attacked Israel's ally Gibeon, Joshua marched all night to help. God threw the enemy into confusion and fought for Israel with great hailstones. Joshua prayed, and the sun stood still until the battle was won. There was no day like it, for the LORD fought for Israel.

When Joshua was old, he gathered Israel's leaders for a farewell. He reminded them how God had fought for them and kept every promise. He urged them to hold fast to the LORD and love Him. They were not to turn aside to other gods.

Joshua called the people to choose whom they would serve. "As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD," he declared. The people answered that they too would serve the LORD, who had done such great things. They remembered how He brought them out of Egypt.

scrambleVerses.text: The LORD our God will we serve,
Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage:
but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

triviaQuestions.question: What miracle happened as Joshua fought for Gibeon?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Joshua 10:13 — "And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day."

triviaQuestions.question: "As for me and my house, we will serve the ___."
triviaQuestions.explanation: Joshua 24:15 — "And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."

triviaQuestions.question: What did the aged Joshua tell Israel to be very courageous to keep?
options: All that is written in the book of the law of Moses
triviaQuestions.explanation: Joshua 23:6 — "Be ye therefore very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that ye turn not aside therefrom to the right hand or to the left;"

triviaQuestions.question: How did the people answer when Joshua told them to choose?
options: They asked for more time to decide
They chose the gods of the Amorites
They said, God forbid that we should forsake the LORD
They went back over the Jordan
triviaQuestions.explanation: Joshua 24:16 — "And the people answered and said, God forbid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods;"

reflection: Joshua made his choice public: 'as for me and my house.' What would it look like to choose the LORD for your home?
